target.title: fix(gateway): evaluate channel health at startup grace
target.body:
Closes #105668

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where gateway operators with dead or unauthenticated channels would wait a full health-monitor interval (default 5 minutes) after startup before the first automatic recovery evaluation, even though the configured startup grace is only 60 seconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

When startup grace is shorter than the check interval (the production default), the monitor now arms a one-shot evaluation at grace expiry in addition to the existing interval cadence. Interval ticks during grace remain no-ops via the existing `startedAt` gate. Stop/shutdown/abort still clear both timers.

## User Impact

Gateways recover stale/dead channel accounts sooner after process start: first health evaluation runs at startup-grace expiry instead of waiting for the first full interval tick. No config changes.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Commands:
```text
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.ts src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts
```

Results:
- `git diff --check`: pass
- `oxfmt --check` on touched files: pass
- focused Vitest: **184 passed** (4 gateway project shards × 46 tests), including new case `runs first health check at startup grace without waiting for the full interval`

Closeout note: `pnpm check:changed` expanded into long-running `tsgo:core:test` (>25m CPU-heavy); substituted path-scoped format check + focused Vitest for the touched surface.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Channel health monitor performs its first post-grace evaluation at startup-grace expiry when grace is shorter than the check interval, instead of waiting for the first full interval tick.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout; Vitest fake timers; `src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts`.
- Current-main contrast: On main, `startChannelHealthMonitor` only arms `setInterval(checkIntervalMs)`. With defaults (60s grace, 5m interval), no evaluation is scheduled until 5 minutes after start even though grace ends at 60s. The new regression test with `startupGraceMs: 1_000` and `checkIntervalMs: 60_000` fails on that schedule (no snapshot at t=1s).
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts`
  2. Case `runs first health check at startup grace without waiting for the full interval` advances timers by 1001ms with grace=1s and interval=60s and asserts `getRuntimeSnapshot` was called once; a further 10s advance does not call again until the interval.
- Evidence after fix: focused suite green, 184/184 tests passed; new first-check-at-grace case passes.
- Control check: Existing cases still prove no evaluation before grace (`does not run before the grace period`), steady interval cadence, cooldown, single-flight, and stop/abort cleanup.
- Observed result after fix: First evaluation fires at startup-grace expiry when grace < interval; later cadence remains the configured interval.
- What was not tested: Live multi-channel gateway with intentionally dead Telegram/Slack tokens across a real 60s grace / 5m interval wall-clock boot (covered at source with fake timers instead).

## AI disclosure

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Grok / find-openclaw-issue + fix-openclaw-issue auto pipeline). Human operator did not manually edit the diff.
